decisions.title: Adopt a content-pinned exception for exactly eight ratified DEC-7201 updater files
decisions.decision: Adopt the fixed-baseline, content-and-mode-pinned legacy exception for exactly the eight paths in sps2/governance/legacy-exception-manifest.json. The manifest canonical SHA-256 is sha256:71a054df3f0fa884dae450d2bd7a586318c6bbb3624e0138fbf9442916a8891d and its authority baseline is c49f3852e1c31d0136269c80fe58201b059af3ec. A path is exempt only when the manifest is present, parseable, hash-verified, and internally exact; the path appears exactly once; it is repository-relative and contained; lstat shows a regular non-symlink file; its worktree blob, SHA-256, and mode equal the manifest values; and its stage-0 blob equals either the authority-baseline blob or the expected worktree blob. Any third stage-0 value, missing entry, deletion, rename, type change, mode change, content change, duplicate, ninth path, or excluded check-update mirror change fails. The P5 checker uses the same shared exception while preserving its c11da27 enumeration scope and fail-closed behavior. This narrowly supersedes only the conflicting legacy-diff-zero scope of DEC-0028, REQ-P3-08, REQ-P9-10, D-P7-C, the P7/P9 threat models, and the P10 roadmap prohibition for these eight pinned files; historical D-P7-C and historical P2 evidence are not rewritten.
decisions.reason: The User explicitly approved the corrected eight-path exception, manifest integrity contract, exclusion of all four check-update mirrors, and P5 shared-exception treatment while preserving the fail-closed legacy-preservation intent.

This differs from Round 25 because scripts/sps-update.sh, its mirror, and sps2/tests/test_updater_safety.py changed after Round 25 as authorized updater-safety work.

decisions.title: Permit exactly four pinned P10 Home imports from the P9 SEO engine
decisions.decision: Adopt the exact four file/module/source-symbol groups in sps2/governance/p10-p9-import-exception-manifest.json. The manifest canonical SHA-256 is sha256:d8dd50395689de0325c29fd55ea959205bee17b9a606b84b236fd3f044f22448 and its authority baseline is c49f3852e1c31d0136269c80fe58201b059af3ec. A compliant import is an absolute ast.ImportFrom whose canonical source file, source module, and imported source symbol exactly match an approved group; a local alias is irrelevant. Module imports, aliased module imports, star imports, unlisted files, modules, or symbols, duplicate source symbols, dynamic imports, syntax-invalid files, symlinked files, path traversal, and paths outside the root remain forbidden. A shared scanner is used by both P9 isolation and rollback. The four groups are owned P10 dependencies, not rollback orphans; P9 removal is a coordinated architectural operation and is no longer guaranteed to leave Home buildable until the dependency is retired or migrated. Every other domain.seo reference outside the P9 surface remains forbidden.
decisions.reason: The User explicitly approved only the four Home/P9 groups, the manifest integrity and strict scanner rules, and the P9 rollback amendment recognizing the owned Home dependency.

decisions.decision: Adopt anchored compatibility for historical identifiers matching DEC-#### or D-P<phase>-<UPPERCASE_ALNUM_SEGMENTS>. New decision records MUST use DEC-####. Historical D-P* identifiers remain compatibility-only, retain their provenance, and gain no approval validity. JSON Schema and every Python validator SHALL use the equivalent anchored pattern; duplicate-ID checks and all reason, evidence, attribution, and approval rules remain mandatory. Validator process exit semantics remain unchanged: decision-data errors are reported visibly without changing the existing exit-code contract.
